title: An area bound limits a detached G2874 companion-cloud eclipse to 8.88 years in the stated range
abstract: We prove a swept-area bound on eclipses by a detached cloud around a companion on a Kepler orbit. The bound covers every eccentricity, inclination and direction of pericenter. For a cloud inside a fixed pericenter Hill-size sphere, a necessary depth condition gives a bound across continuous parameter ranges. A primary mass of at least 0.8 solar masses, stellar radius of at most 1.5 solar radii, companion mass up to 80 Jupiter masses, and apocenter up to 11.91 au give less than 8.88 years of possible overlap per orbit. The model must reach 0.30 mag with maximum surface intensity at most twice the disc mean. One 19-year eclipse instead needs apocenter above 19.79 au in this range. The nominal 80-Jupiter case improves a prior analytic bound from 14.961 to 7.7385 years. Exact contacts for 19,114 random orbits check the code. This is a conditional theorem, not new photometry. Sparse G2874 plates do not prove continuous obscuration, and grain models do not establish an upper companion distance. The proof does not show that circular orbits maximize duration. Original code, proof, aggregate tables, source hashes and figures are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-4b8d04cea9f1; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
